meta.title: Spectrum occupancy survey of the WSPR sub-bands
meta.tools: wspr.live database, NumPy statistics (occupancy histograms, hourly load)
meta.summary: Measure how the 200 Hz-wide WSPR segment of each amateur band is actually used: frequency occupancy within the segment, hourly load and the fraction of transmitters on crowded vs quiet slots, from one day of real reports.
meta.problem: Spectrum is shared by thousands of independent users. How evenly do they spread across the available channel, and how busy is it through the day?
meta.theory:
If N transmitters pick frequencies uniformly in a 200 Hz segment and each WSPR signal occupies ~6 Hz, the expected fraction
of time-frequency overlap (collisions) for a given transmission is $\approx1-e^{-N\cdot 6/200}$ per 2-minute slot (Poisson). Users
cluster around the segment centre, so the real occupancy histogram is peaked, raising collisions above the uniform
estimate.
meta.method:
Spots on 20 m, 2026-09-10: frequency offset within 14.0970–14.0972 MHz in 5 Hz bins (unique transmitter/slot pairs); per
2-minute slot, each transmitter's frequency = median over all receivers that heard it; fraction of transmitters with
another transmitter within ±6 Hz vs the uniform Poisson estimate.

rows.quantity: Fraction of transmissions within 6 Hz of another (uniform-spread Poisson)

metrics.quantity: Mean distinct transmitters per slot (20 m)
